title: Repair candidate retrieval before buying a lower alert threshold
observed_evidence: 909/6,000 held-out aliases scored zero in the historical blocked pipeline. A fixture demonstrates a greater-than-90 similarity match lost by prefix blocking; this is a retrieval defect, not an impossibility bound.
executive_recommendation: Prioritize recall diagnostics and secondary identifiers. Neither low alert volume nor a high similarity threshold establishes identity or compliance.
priorities: Separate retrieval recall from conditional scoring recall at entity level.
Compare additional alert workload with staffed review capacity before expanding retrieval.
Prespecify identity-labeled negative evaluation and escalation rules; keep unresolved cases unresolved.
reversal: If expanded retrieval exceeds review capacity or fails the missed-identity gate, increase capacity or hold deployment instead of hiding risk by raising the threshold.
uncertainty: Historical negatives are not identity-adjudicated ground truth; expected losses and incident rates here are scenario values, not legal or financial forecasts.

economics.evidence_status: ILLUSTRATIVE ASSUMPTIONS, NOT MEASURED COSTS OR RISK

product.randomization_unit: screening reviewer; cluster by entity/team when cases repeat
product.retention_interpretation: reviewer returns for another eligible screening queue
